title: The Sixteenth Mixtape
premise: Sebastian Hartwell has spent a decade as the invisible statistician of the Hollow Creek swim team, quietly logging the impossible times that prove Coach Danner is doping his athletes—times he's kept secret because exposing them would destroy his best friend Marcus, the team's star. When Marcus vanishes after confronting Danner, leaving only a set of keys and an unfinished mixtape labeled 'sixteen,' Sebastian must finally break his silence. As he follows the tape's clues through the town's complicit adults, he discovers Marcus didn't run—he was silenced—and that Danner's web of influence reaches the police and Sebastian's own family. In the end, Sebastian testifies at the hearing knowing it will cost him his scholarship, his standing, and any hope of belonging again, but Marcus's recovered testimony proves the truth was worth every price.
about_author: C. M. Underhill is a former high school athletic department volunteer who spent three years watching small-town sports culture from the sidelines before writing about it. They live in the Pacific Northwest with two rescue dogs and an ever-growing collection of unlabeled cassette tapes.

chapters.title: The Keys on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. When Marcus misses their annual championship-eve tradition, Sebastian finds his friend's house empty, keys abandoned, and a cassette marked 'sixteen' hidden in the stat room. Playing it, he hears Marcus's frightened voice hinting at 'the numbers' before cutting off. The emotional beat: dread crystallizing into guilt—Sebastian realizes he knew the data was wrong for years and said nothing.

chapters.title: What the Numbers Knew
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, alternating flashbacks to ten years of careful silence. He digs into his old spreadsheets and finds Marcus's name flagged alongside three athletes who transferred away abruptly. When he approaches the assistant coach, she warns him off with genuine fear. The beat: rising tension as Sebastian understands the conspiracy is bigger than one coach, and that asking questions made him visible—and vulnerable—for the first time.

chapters.title: Sixteen Reasons to Stay Quiet
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Following the mixtape's track list—each song title a clue—he finds Marcus hiding in the boathouse, injured but alive, too terrified to testify because Danner holds evidence against his family. Meanwhile Danner offers Sebastian a college sponsorship to stay silent. The climax: Sebastian chooses truth over safety, copying the files and calling the state investigator, burning every bridge of belonging he has left.

chapters.title: Louder Than the Crowd
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, weeks later at the disciplinary hearing. His testimony costs him the scholarship and his father's approval, but Marcus corroborates from the stand, and Danner is barred for life. The team dissolves; some teammates never forgive him. The resolution: on the pool deck, Marcus hands Sebastian a new tape labeled 'seventeen'—proof that real belonging isn't given by institutions but chosen by the people who stay.
